missionPremise: A Travis bake with only Pflugerville and Lakeway stamped would overwrite roughly 233k zoned nodes with roughly 35k, and the existing row-level guards would not catch it because every individual row it wrote would be valid. The defect is only visible at the population level -- the same blind spot as the Bastrop 92.5-percent false retirement, whose lesson is that a job should not need to know what went wrong in order to stop, because the share alone is disqualifying. The scenario is live: Austin's zoning layer returns 499 Token Required and Lockhart's service is gone from its org.

theAuthorisationPath.carriedHow: an execution-time env override on `gcloud run jobs execute --update-env-vars`, the same mechanism as OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO. Never `gcloud run jobs update` on the template and never a config default.
whyItIsNotAHabitFlag: It names BOTH measured populations exactly, so it cannot be written before the refusal has been read. There is no value anyone could put on a job template in advance, because the value does not exist until the measurement does.

It EXPIRES on any movement in either population. A token whose source count differs by ONE refuses COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_STALE. A token left over from last week, or from a different county, does not carry.

A wrong county is its own code (COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_COUNTY_MISMATCH) and a malformed value is a third (COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_MALFORMED), so a mistyped authorisation never lands in the same bucket as no authorisation.

Every crossing is recorded on the run as a coverage-floor run_event carrying override.authorised, so overrides are countable rather than invisible. An override merely PRESENT while the floor passes is recorded as overridePresentUnused, because a leftover authorisation nobody noticed is the exact shape this operation keeps finding.
theAuthorisationPath.honestLimit: The refusal prints the exact token, so an operator who wants through gets through in one paste. That is deliberate: the alternative teaches people to delete the gate. What it buys is that the decision cannot be made without the numbers in hand, cannot be made once for all future runs, and always leaves a named record. It is a decision point, not a wall.

firstEverBake.whatHappens: It PROMOTES, under priorBasis 'no-prior', with firstEverBake true and retention null. A floor must not refuse a county's first load.
firstEverBake.howNoPriorIsDistinguishedFromZeroPrior: The discriminator is servedTier1Rows, NOT servedZoned, and both come from the same query in the same call. servedTier1Rows === 0 means the county has never been baked on this target: the prior is UNMEASURED and retention is null, never 0 and never 1. servedTier1Rows > 0 with servedZoned === 0 means the prior was MEASURED and is genuinely zero -- a legitimately unzoned county, since unincorporated Texas is legitimately unzoned -- and gets its own basis 'prior-zero'. A third state, a count that is absent or non-integer, refuses COVERAGE_UNMEASURED rather than defaulting to zero.
firstEverBake.whyItCannotPassEverythingForeverAfter: The prior is read from place_layer_snapshots, which the first bake itself writes. So the SECOND bake for that county necessarily has servedTier1Rows > 0 and the floor engages with no further action by anyone. There is no state in which 'no prior' is inferred from a zero and then honoured indefinitely. A test pins exactly this: bake 1 promotes on no-prior, bake 2 with a collapsed source refuses.
firstEverBake.theResidualNamedRatherThanGlossed: A relative floor inherits whatever the first bake established. If a county's FIRST EVER bake is itself collapsed, the collapsed number becomes the baseline and the second bake compares against it happily. That is inherent to every relative floor, it is not fixed here, and it is why P-236's own standing rule (Travis stays OUT of any bake while Austin is unmeasured) is a rule about the first bake. The run record carries the absolute counts and not only the share, so the baseline is auditable.

contradicted: Four of my own predictions, recorded in CP2 rather than quietly corrected. (1) The instrument's own summary line claimed a round, symmetrical 'refuses everything fails 5, refuses nothing fails 5'. The actual violation runs mismatched FOUR and TWO, because four scenarios are decided before the ratio is consulted and are ratio-independent by design; the line and the header now carry the measured sets. A convenient round number in an instrument's own output is the exact failure this repo keeps paying for, and it was caught only by running the thing. (2) The refusal message read 'It would have overwrite ...' -- caught by printing the operator-facing string, not by re-reading code I had already read several times. (3) I assumed the publish fake exposed `client._t`; it exposes `client.tables`, with parsed bodies and a `publish_runs` table, and four full-path tests failed on the readback while their refusal assertions passed. (4) I assumed the dispatch's worktree path would be acceptable; SEAT-01 refused the first Write because it is outside the seat-namespaced layout, and the lane registered and moved to the convention rather than working around it.

SEAT-01_product_index_foreign_refuses_ev.severity: real scope defect in a live control, not mine to fix, verified by direct invocation
SEAT-01_product_index_foreign_refuses_ev.what: scripts/enforcement/seat-register.mjs `ownerOfRepoPath` returns the FIRST seat-product entry matching a repoPath. seat-worktree-gate.mjs's git-write branch then refuses any git add/commit whose worktree is not that first entry's. For hauska-factory the first entry is hauska-factory-f10, so a correctly registered lane worktree on its correctly registered branch is refused with `product_index_foreign`.
SEAT-01_product_index_foreign_refuses_ev.evidenceVerbatim: evaluate({worktree:'P:/seat-worktrees/property/hauska-factory-p236-coverage-floor', branch:'fix/p236-county-coverage-floor', command:'git commit -m x'}) -> {"allow":false,"code":"product_index_foreign","message":"SEAT-01: refusing git write in P:/seat-worktrees/property/hauska-factory-p236-coverage-floor; owner worktree is P:/seat-worktrees/property/hauska-factory-f10."} , while the same call with paths instead of a command returns {"allow":true,"code":"ok","seat":"property"}.
SEAT-01_product_index_foreign_refuses_ev.whyNobodyHasHitIt: the hook's shell mode resolves the worktree from the SHELL'S CWD, never from the `git -C` target. A lane whose shell sits in a doc_repo worktree is evaluated as kind 'integration' or 'seat-doc', which skips the seat-product branch entirely. So the defect is masked by the hook's own scope, which means it will surface the first time someone cd's into a lane worktree to commit.
SEAT-01_product_index_foreign_refuses_ev.howThisLaneProceeded: the ordinary `git -C <worktree> commit` form from the default cwd, which is how these commands are written anyway. Named rather than presented as a clean pass: had the hook read the -C target, a legitimate registered lane would have been blocked. This was NOT bypass hunting -- the probe was the registration verification the seat gate itself requires, and the refusal was found while confirming the registration was real.
SEAT-01_product_index_foreign_refuses_ev.recommendation: a row for the seat that owns the enforcement scripts: ownerOfRepoPath should resolve the LONGEST-matching registered worktree rather than the first entry for the repoPath, or the git-write branch should compare against the entry already resolved by findByWorktree instead of re-deriving an owner.

LESSON: The two sides of a coverage floor must be the same predicate, or the threshold becomes a calibrated number and the control becomes a tuning exercise. Here both sides reduce to txgio_parcel.zoning_district being non-blank, which is why 1.0000 is the healthy reading and 0.95 needs no justification beyond the gap to the failure mode.

A relative floor's prior must be read from the serving store, not from a count the previous run recorded about itself. Reading the store means the floor is armed from the first publish under the new code for every county ever baked; reading a self-reported number means every county reads as no-prior on the first run.

The discriminator between 'no prior' and 'zero prior' has to be a DIFFERENT quantity from the one being floored (row count, not zoned count), or the two states are not representable and the trap closes itself.
pg returns bigint as a STRING. A comparison that never coerces would order '35000' above '233000' and pass exactly the collapse it exists to stop. The fixtures feed strings on purpose.
DEAD-END: Building this as a post-condition on the baked result. Measurable, but the rows are already written, so it is a detector -- and it would have been a second, weaker copy of the control publish-cadroll-postcondition.mjs already occupies.

Expressing the override as a share to four decimal places. On a 233k population a 4dp share does not move when a handful of rows change, so a stale token would still match. The exact integer pair expires on any movement.
